rows.text: The load nut's wear indicator must be checked every 6 months, according to section 7.3 (Checking the Load Nut's Wear Indicator) of the MA STAR two post lift operating instructions.

Universal Robots recommends unpacking and starting up a UR10e kept in long-term storage (6 months or more) at least yearly, then running a light load program that rotates all joints at least 90 degrees 5 times in each direction. This is in the Long Term Storage guidance (section 17.4 in the UR10e manual's table of contents).
The manufacturer states a mission time TM of 20 years (ISO 13849) for both the nanoScan3 Core I/O and Pro I/O in the safety-related parameters table on page 130 (continuing Table 34).
The UR5e manual (Section 4, Safety, WARNING: HOT SURFACE, p. 33) says to allow the robot to cool down by powering it off and waiting one hour before handling it.

The UNIVPM guideline passages (p. 4, 6 and 7) do not state how long check results must be kept for the supervisory bodies. A three-year retention period for the last three years of results appears in a different guideline (UNICT, p. 18, comma 9), not in the UNIVPM text.

No. The UR10e is a partly completed machine under the Machinery Directive, so the manufacturer does not affix a CE mark (manual chapter 20, p. 229). The integrator must apply the CE mark and issue the Declaration of Conformity once the robot is built into a complete machine, as stated in the Declaration of Incorporation (2006/42/EC Annex II B, p. 227).

No. Section 2.3 (Improper use) of the nanoScan3 manual lists 'Outdoors' under impermissible ambient conditions, and section 2.2 says the scanner must only be used within the prescribed operating conditions.

Yes. Section 10.3.3 (Safety Configuration without Teach Pendant, UR10e manual p. 126) states the robot can be used without attaching the Teach Pendant, provided another Emergency Stop source is defined. Detaching the Teach Pendant deactivates its Emergency Stop button, so it must be removed from the robot's vicinity.

value: after changes to the configuration or the safety function
after changes to the mounting, the alignment, or the electrical connection
after exceptional events, such as detected manipulation, modification of the machine, or replacement of components
rows.text: Section 5.6.1 (nanoscan3 manual, p. 50) requires a thorough check of the protective device and its application before commissioning, after changes to the configuration or safety function, after changes to mounting, alignment, or electrical connection, and after exceptional events such as detected manipulation, machine modification, or component replacement.

rows.value: The integrator is responsible for the application risk assessment; the user can also be the integrator.
rows.text: According to the UR10e manual, Section 14 (Risk Assessment, passage 0, p. 186), the application risk assessment is the responsibility of the integrator, and the user may also be the integrator. Section 4.4 (passage 2, p. 34) likewise assigns the risk assessment for the complete robot system to the person(s) integrating the UR robot.

The passages describe how to replace the Control Box filters (section 18, Maintenance and Repair, figure 3.7 in the UR10e manual) but do not state how often they must be replaced. The provided passages do not give a replacement interval.

The passages do not record when the cell's nanoScan3 was last checked. Passage 5 (manual section 5) says the regular thorough check must be carried out at least once a year, but no check date is given for this installation.

The passages do not state how often the UR5e must be recalibrated. Section 18 (Maintenance and Repair) says calibration must follow the manual's safety instructions and the UR Service Manual, and its inspection checklist lists monthly, biannual and annual timeframes for inspections, not recalibration. Section 18.1 says stopping performance should be tested periodically, without a set interval.

The passages place crane 13 in table A2 (overhead travelling cranes, positions 8-13) and say verification follows Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08, but they do not state whether that crane is mobile/transferable or fixed, or its year of manufacture, which set the interval. For extractive-sector cranes over 200 kg, Allegato VII gives annual verification for mobile or transferable cranes, and for fixed cranes it gives annual if built more than 10 years ago and biennial if not.

The passages do not mention a DEFRIES-TITANO crane or a position 11, so its verification frequency cannot be determined from them. For general context, the Allegato VII extracts in passages 6 and 8 set annual verification for mobile or transferable cranes over 200 kg used in extractive-sector settings, and for fixed cranes in those settings that are more than 10 years old; a fixed extractive-sector crane under 10 years old is verified biennially. Confirming the crane's type, age, and sector would be needed to apply these rules.

The passages do not mention an AMCO VEBA crane or a position 4 crane with a 520 kg capacity, so they do not set a verification frequency for it. The truck-crane entries in the Igea technical sheet (passage 8) concern a different owner's fleet, and the general verification tables in Allegato VII (passage 1) do not identify a specific crane by make, position, or capacity.

rows.value: Biennial (every 2 years) if built within the last 10 years; annual if built more than 10 years ago. The Allegato VII row 18 triennial rule covers fixed equipment and does not apply to a mobile crane.
rows.text: For a mobile lifting appliance over 200 kg used outside the construction, steel, port and extractive sectors, Allegato VII of D.lgs. 81/2008 requires a biennial check if manufactured no earlier than 10 years ago, and an annual check if older. The passages do not give the JS190NLC's manufacture year, so the exact interval cannot be determined; the triennial entry at position 18 is for fixed equipment.

The passages do not give the manufacturing year or the mobile/fixed classification of crane position 13 (table A2, Allegato A, not included). Under Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08 (art. 71 c. 11), outside the construction, steel, port and extractive sectors the interval is biennial or triennial for fixed cranes, and biennial or annual for mobile/transferable cranes, depending on whether the crane is more or less than 10 years old.

The passages do not identify the GUTTER crane at position 10 or give its age, load rating, or whether it is mobile or fixed, so its verification interval cannot be determined. Allegato VII (art. 71, c. 11) sets, for lifting equipment over 200 kg outside the construction, steel, port and extractive sectors, a biennial check if it was made no earlier than 10 years ago and an annual check if it was made more than 10 years ago.
In Annex B, Table B3 (passage 0), the lifting devices located in Lula (Sos Enattos) are at positions 3 (hydraulic crane FASSI on IVECO truck) and 23 (A-frame crane GCB 35 X, serial 459).

The appointed verifier must plan the device checks jointly with IGEA's appointed staff and notify IGEA at least 15 days in advance (Scheda Tecnica, section 4 'Impegni Aggiudicatario/Verificatore', igea-equipment p. 5).

No. Under point 4.2.1 of the IGEA Scheda Tecnica, IGEA must provide the verifier with the necessary personnel under a supervisor and the means for the operations (test weights), but this expressly excludes measuring instruments (apparecchi di misurazione).

rows.value: ASL (local health authorities); within 30 days of the request
rows.text: Under Article 2(1) of the Ministerial Decree of 11 April 2011, the ASL (local health authority) is responsible for the periodic verifications after the first one, and these must be carried out within 30 days of the request.

The passages define a supplementary investigation (Allegato II, section 2.c of DM 11 April 2011) as applying to equipment in service for over 20 years, but they do not say whether the employer must show its results during periodic verification, and they do not mention the P&H R200 crane or position 17.

The passages do not give the last verification date for the DEMAG overhead travelling crane at position 9. Passage 3 places positions 8-13 in the group of overhead travelling cranes (gru a ponte scorrevole) and says the dates of the last verifications are in Allegato A, table A2, but that table is not included. No passage names DEMAG.

The passages do not mention a P&H R200 crane, position 17, or any record of its last periodic verification, so overdue status cannot be determined. Passage 0 (Allegato VII) gives verification frequencies for mobile lifting equipment over 200 kg, which depend on sector and age, but the crane's sector, manufacture year, and last verification date are not provided.

Position 13 is a gru a ponte scorrevole in Table A2 of Allegato A, at a mining site (passage 0). The passages do not say whether it is mobile/transferable or fixed, or when it was built, and Allegato VII (passages 5 and 9) sets the interval by those factors: annual for mobile/transferable cranes over 200 kg in the extractive sector, and for fixed cranes built more than 10 years earlier; biennial for fixed cranes built within 10 years. The date 1 June 2027 does not change this.

The passages do not give a definite answer. Position 13 is a travelling overhead crane in table A2 (positions 8-13), and the company operates in mining areas (Art. 2.2, Allegato B). Under the Allegato VII periodicity in the passages, a fixed lifting appliance over 200 kg used in the extractive sector is verified annually if its manufacture year is more than 10 years old, and biennially if it is 10 years old or less. Table A2 and the manufacture year of position 13 are not in the passages, so the 2028 frequency cannot be confirmed. Please check table A2 and Allegato B for position 13's year of manufacture and whether it is fixed or mobile/transferable.

The passages do not mention the FASSI F 28 B22 crane or its year of manufacture. For a mobile or transferable lifting device over 200 kg used regularly outside the construction, steel, port and extractive sectors, Annex VII requires verification every two years if it was manufactured within the last 10 years, and every year if it was manufactured more than 10 years ago (Allegato VII, mobile/transferable rows for other sectors). Without the crane's manufacturing year, the 2018 frequency cannot be determined from these passages.

The passages give the rule for mobile lifting equipment over 200 kg used outside the construction, steel, port and extractive sectors: verification is biennial if the year of manufacture is not more than 10 years old (Allegato VII, per passages 2 and 3), and annual if it is older. The passages do not give the crane's year of manufacture, so the verification frequency for this crane cannot be determined.

Position 7 is a truck-mounted crane in the Igea S.p.A. fleet (Allegato A, table A1), and Passage 1 places the cranes in mining areas, so the Allegato VII extractive-sector rule for mobile lifting equipment over 200 kg applies: annual verification, with no age condition listed. The passages do not name Effer or the crane's year of manufacture, so the age-based alternatives cannot be checked.

Position 13 is a gru a ponte scorrevole (overhead travelling crane) in Igea's table A2, but the passages do not include table A2 or give its manufacture year or whether it is fixed or mobile. Under Allegato VII, outside the construction, steel, port and extractive sectors, the interval is triennial or biennial for a fixed crane and biennial or annual for a mobile one, depending on whether it is less or more than 10 years old, so the 2031 frequency cannot be determined from these passages (see Allegato VII table, unict-guideline p. 19, and inail-guide p. 34).

Under Allegato VII, row 16 of D.Lgs. 81/2008, fixed lifting appliances over 200 kg used in extractive and other listed sectors, manufactured no more than 10 years earlier, require a biennial verification. The passages do not state whether the KITO KR50L is fixed or its manufacturing year, so if it is older than 10 years the annual interval (Verifica annuale, same allegato) would apply instead.

The passages do not confirm which category the gantry crane falls under. Under Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/2008 (passages 2 and 8), lifting appliances over 200 kg used in the extractive sector need an annual check if they are mobile or transferable, and this applies regardless of age. If the crane is fixed, the interval depends on its manufacture year: annual if built more than 10 years ago, biennial if not. The passages do not say whether this gantry crane is mobile or fixed or when it was built.

The passages do not mention the SIS PROFI 10 TI, position 14, whether the hoist is mobile or fixed, or its year of manufacture, so the interval cannot be determined. Under Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/2008, outside the construction, steel, port and extractive sectors, a mobile or transferable hoist over 200 kg needs verification every two years if built within the last 10 years and annually if older, while a fixed one needs it every three years if built within the last 10 years and every two years if older.

Positions 8 to 12 (Allegato A, Tabella A2, overhead bridge cranes built 1978 to 1988), position 17 (Allegato A, Tabella A4, P&H autogru built 1977) and position 23 (Allegato A, Tabella A5, Euro costruzioni Pellegrini crane built 1989) have a construction year earlier than 1990. The Allegato B location tables show the same years for these positions.

The passages do not identify any list position with a capacity below 1,000 kg. The load-control requirement (Annex I, 4.2.2 and Annex III, 4.2.2) applies at 1,000 kg or more, and the list in passage 8 covers lifting appliances above 200 kg, which does not establish a capacity below 1,000 kg.
In Annex B, Table B1 (igea-equipment, p. 8), positions 13 and 14 list Monteponi in the sector/service column. The text is garbled by OCR, so the column assignment is inferred from the row order.

The passages state that IGEA must provide the structural verification certificate for residual life cycles for equipment over 20 years old (Scheda Tecnica, p. 5, document list item 5), and that the seven truck-mounted cranes are positions 1-7 in Allegato A, table A1 (p. 3). They do not give the manufacture or age data in table A1, so they cannot show which of those cranes exceed 20 years.

The passages do not state how long an authorised body must keep verification documents under the Ministerial Decree of 11 April 2011. Passage 6 (IGEA equipment technical sheet) refers to that decree for the verification procedures but gives no retention period.

The passages identify the Effer 790 crane at position 7 (Annex A, Table A1, and Annex B, Table B1, of the igea-equipment document) and name the truck make as FIAT, but they give no registration plate for that truck. The plate field in that row is empty, unlike the other crane rows, which list plates.

The passages identify position 23 as a gantry crane (gru a cavalletto, table A5 of Allegato A in the Igea technical sheet, passage 7), but they give no euro amount. They refer only to the tariff in the INAIL decree of 23 November 2012 for periodic verification of Allegato VII equipment (passages 0 and 2), and do not state the 35,000 kg crane's fee.

Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 governs placing on the market. Under Art. 52(1), Directive 2006/42/EC covers only products placed on the market in conformity with it before 14 January 2027, and this machine is first made available on 25 January 2027, after that date. The signing date of 10 January 2027 does not determine the governing act.

Under Article 12(4) of Directive 2006/42/EC, machinery in Annex IV that is not built to harmonised standards may use only the EC type-examination procedure (Annex IX, plus internal checks under Annex VIII point 3) or full quality assurance (Annex X). Unit verification (module G) is not listed. The passages do not give the Regulation's application date, so they cannot confirm that the Regulation applies on 1 December 2026. Its Article 25 provides for module G only for categories in its own Annex I.

The passages do not state any date-based change for module A on 1 February 2027. Article 25(3) of the Machinery Regulation allows internal production control (module A) for Annex I Part B categories only when the machinery is designed and constructed to the applicable harmonised standards or common specifications, but they set no cut-off date.

Under Article 18 of the Machinery Regulation (REG), a company that substantially modifies machinery is considered a manufacturer and must meet the Article 10 manufacturer obligations. The passages do not state the Regulation's date of application, so they do not confirm that it governs a modification on 1 March 2027.

Yes. Under Art. 10(7) of the Regulation, the manufacturer may provide digital instructions if it marks how to access them, makes them printable and downloadable, and keeps them online for at least 10 years, and it must supply paper only if the user requests it at purchase (free, within one month); the UNIVPM guideline's paper-only statement (p. 7, section 4) relies on the superseded Directive 2006/42/CE and conflicts with this.

The passages do not state when the Machinery Regulation (REG) or Directive 2006/42/EC (DIR) applies, so they cannot establish which act governs on 1 March 2027. If the Regulation applies that day, Article 15(2)(a)-(d) would require the distributor to verify the CE marking, the EU declaration of conformity (Article 10(8)), the instructions for use and information (Article 10(7)) in a language users can easily understand, and that the manufacturer and importer complied with Article 10(5)-(6) and Article 13(3).

Under Article 52(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Member States may not impede making available machinery placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 14 January 2027, so the last qualifying placing-on-the-market day is 13 January 2027.
Article 6(7) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies from 13 July 2023, as set out in Article 54(c).

Under Article 53(3) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, the first specific report was due by 14 July 2026, and the next falls every five years after that. The second report on the assessment of Article 6(4) and (5) is therefore due by 14 July 2031.

No. Under Article 47(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, the delegation runs for five years from 13 July 2023, so it ends on 13 July 2028. The Commission must draw up its report no later than nine months before that end date, which is 13 October 2027. That deadline has not yet passed as of 14 November 2026.

No. The UR10e Declaration of Incorporation (Section 20.1, p. 227, made under 2006/42/EC Annex II B) states that the arm shall only be put into service after it is integrated into a final complete machine or cell that conforms to the Machinery Directive and other applicable Directives. The integrator is responsible for that conformity, the CE mark, and the Declaration of Conformity.

rows.value: The technical file for the final machinery
rows.text: Under Article 13(2) of Directive 2006/42/EC, the assembly instructions and the declaration of incorporation accompany the partly completed machinery until it is incorporated into the final machinery, and then form part of that machinery's technical file.

The passages do not contain the text of Article 5(1) of any act, so they cannot say what it requires. They do describe integrator duties in the UR manuals and Declarations of Incorporation: a risk assessment for the complete system (manual p. 31/186), and under the Declaration of Incorporation, the integrator making the completed machine conform with all applicable Directives, applying the CE mark and providing the Declaration of Conformity.

The passages do not say whether this lift unit falls under the machinery rules, when those rules apply, or which conformity assessment procedure the manufacturer used. Article 24(3) of the Machinery Regulation requires the notified body's identification number only where the procedure is one listed in Article 25(2)(a), (b) or (c) or Article 25(3)(b), (c) or (d), and none of the passages establishes that either condition is met.
The passages do not address Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 or any Italian penalty rules for it, so the maximum penalty cannot be determined from them.

The passages state only that the first implementing act under Article 6(10) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 had to be adopted not later than 14 July 2024. They do not say when the Commission actually adopted it.

The passages do not name the notified body that carried out the EC type-examination of the MA STAR two post lift. The MAHA EC Declaration of Conformity (passage 0) gives no notified body, and Annex IX of the Machinery Directive (passage 2) describes the procedure only in general terms.

The passages do not give a date for the EC declaration of conformity of a complete robot cell. The UR5e and UR10e declaration of incorporation (ur10e-manual p. 227, ur5e-manual p. 220) says the integrator must provide the Declaration of Conformity for the completed machine, but it gives no date for that document. The only date in the passages, 25 August 2017, belongs to the environmental assessment, not to a declaration of conformity.

The passages do not state when Article 50(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies. Article 50(1) sets out the Member States' duty to lay down penalties, and Article 50(2) requires notification of those rules to the Commission by 14 October 2026, but neither provision gives an application date.
Articles 26 to 42 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 apply from 14 January 2024, as set out in Article 54(a) of that Regulation.

Under Article 6(9) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Member States must first provide the data and information referred to in Article 6(5) by 14 July 2025, and every five years after that. Article 6(9) sets this date, not Article 6(5) itself.

Under Article 53(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, the Commission must submit its first report on the evaluation and review of the Regulation to the European Parliament and the Council by 14 July 2028, and every four years after that.

No. Article 51(2) of the Regulation repeals Directive 2006/42/EC with effect from 14 January 2027, so it is no longer in force on 18 January 2027. Article 52(1) still lets Member States allow products placed on the market in conformity with the Directive before 14 January 2027 to remain available.
Yes. Article 54(b) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies Article 50(1) (penalties rules) from 14 October 2023, so it already applied on 1 September 2026.

Yes. Article 52(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 says Chapter VI applies mutatis mutandis from 13 July 2023 to products placed on the market under Directive 2006/42/EC, instead of Article 11 of that Directive. Since 15 July 2023 falls after 13 July 2023, Chapter VI already applied on that date.

No. Article 52(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 covers only products placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 14 January 2027. A machine placed on the market on 15 January 2027 falls outside that window, so the date of 1 March 2027 does not bring it within the protection.

No. Under art. 71(11) of D.Lgs. 81/2008, later periodic verifications are at the employer's free choice, from the ASL (or ARPA where regional law provides), or from authorised public or private bodies. The 30-day term in DM 11 April 2011, art. 2(1) is the deadline for the ASL to carry out the verification, and art. 2(8) allows the employer to use authorised bodies once that term has elapsed; the passages do not impose an obligation to apply to the ASL.

Yes. Article 71, paragraph 13-bis of Legislative Decree 81/2008 allows the Corpo nazionale dei vigili del fuoco to carry out the periodic verifications under paragraph 11 directly, for Annex VII equipment it owns or holds on loan, so this carve-out applies instead of the INAIL/ASL allocation. The passages do not confirm that a variable-inclination aerial ladder is listed in Annex VII, so that listing should be checked.

Under Article 52(2) of the Regulation, EC type-examination certificates issued under Article 12 of Directive 2006/42/EC remain valid until they expire. The passages give no fixed end date. Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed with effect from 14 January 2027 under Article 51(2).

The passages do not set a date by which the Commission must adopt the Article 6(11) delegated acts. Article 47(2) (passage 1) confers the power for five years from 13 July 2023, which would run to 13 July 2028 absent tacit extension, but that is the period of delegation, not an adoption deadline. Article 6(11) (passage 9) says only that the acts are adopted 'if necessary after the Commission report referred to in Article 53(3)', with no date.

The passages do not set a time limit for the decree amending the Annex VII equipment list under Article 71(14). Article 71(14) requires the decree but gives no deadline. The 12-month deadline in passage 5 applies to the decree under Article 71(13) on inspection methods and certification criteria, not to Article 71(14).
